name: Every Code

surfaces.label: Every Code interactive terminal UI (`code`, `coder`, `code resume [id]`). One process is one session: the TUI runs the agent loop in-process, there is no shared daemon. The native binary is what runs; the npm `coder` command is a node wrapper (`node .../bin/coder.js`, argv[0]=node, cannot be matched) that spawns it as a direct child, so only the native process matches. Native binary names: code-aarch64-apple-darwin / code-x86_64-apple-darwin (npm cache ~/Library/Caches/just-every/code/<ver>/, node_modules/@just-every/code/bin/, or the platform package @just-every/code-darwin-arm64/bin/), legacy coder-<triple>, or plain `code` (Homebrew tap formula installs the release binary as bin/code; also `cargo`/build-fast.sh output code-rs/target/dev-fast/code).

`code exec` / `code e` headless run (also what Every Code itself spawns for multi-agent /plan /solve /code: `code -s read-only|workspace-write ... exec --skip-git-repo-check ...` as a direct child of the TUI, same binary path, so the probe keeps the outer TUI and drops these). `code auto "goal"` is also headless (main.rs Subcommand::Auto sets auto_drive and runs code_exec::run_main, same as exec) but this surface cannot match it: args_contain is a substring test and a bare `auto` would also hit `--full-auto` and `--auto` on real TUI sessions. It falls to the TUI surface above and is labelled tui; it is alive-means-working in fact, but the TUI signals (rollout tail, direct shell child, CPU) usually catch it too.

`code app-server` and `code mcp-server` (experimental stdio servers for an editor or another agent; hosts threads for a client). `code acp` is NOT this: it is an alias of `code mcp`, the config manager (list/get/add/remove), see notes.

working_signals.name: rollout tail has an open turn
working_signals.meaning: Precise form (from source, no live turn seen): the newest turn-lifecycle record in the rollout is event_msg task_started with no later task_complete or turn_aborted, AND the file was written recently, AND the pid is alive. Every Code persists every event except four (image_generation_begin and three delta kinds), so the file also grows on each exec_command_begin/end and token_count while a turn runs. The rollout file is held open by the process for the whole session (rollout_writer owns the fd), so `lsof -p <pid>` names the file: this maps a process to its transcript without any session id in argv. A quiet file with an open turn is a long model call, a long tool call, an approval wait, or a crashed process; the transcript alone cannot tell which.

A direct shell child (`zsh -c ...` / `bash -lc ...`) exists only while a model-issued shell command runs. Inferred from core/src/shell.rs and seatbelt.rs (`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec ... -- <shell> -lc <cmd>`, sandbox-exec then execs the shell); not seen in a live ps. Blind while the model streams, and blind for apply_patch (in-process). Sub-agent children (`code ... exec`) and browser or MCP children are not shells, so they do not trigger it.

Fallback. There is NO sleep inhibitor in Every Code: no caffeinate child and no IOKit power assertion (0 hits for IOPMAssertion, caffeinate, prevent_idle_sleep in the 0.6.195 binary and none in code-rs), unlike Codex which has an opt-in assertion. CPU is a guess floor; the browser integration and Auto Review worktree agents can add CPU while the main turn is idle.

waiting_signals.meaning: Unlike upstream Codex, Every Code's rollout policy persists these: should_persist_event_msg excludes only ImageGenerationBegin and the AgentMessage/AgentReasoning/AgentReasoningRawContent deltas. So a tail of task_started ... exec_approval_request (or request_user_input) with no later exec_command_begin, task_complete or turn_aborted is a wait on the human. Inferred from source; the JSON wire names are snake_case of the enum variants; no live record was read.
Terminal OSC 9 escape sent for approval-requested and agent-turn-complete. Nothing a process outside the terminal can read.
Runs the program with one JSON argument, but only for agent-turn-complete (that is done, not waiting).
None. There is no approval or notification hook event. The eight hook events (see hooks) cover session, prompt, tool, file write and stop, not permission prompts.

hooks.config: ~/.code/config.toml (legacy ~/.codex/config.toml is also read; CODE_HOME, then CODEX_HOME, override the directory): [[projects."/abs/path".hooks]] tables with event, run or command (string or argv), name, cwd, env, timeout_ms, run_in_background. Hooks are per project path, not global. Env per call: CODE_HOOK_EVENT, CODE_HOOK_NAME, CODE_HOOK_INDEX, CODE_HOOK_CALL_ID, CODE_HOOK_PAYLOAD (JSON), CODE_SESSION_CWD. user.prompt_submit and stop payloads carry session_id, turn_id, transcript_path. Exit 2 with stderr blocks (prompt_submit) or forces a continuation (stop). Separate top-level `notify` fires only for agent-turn-complete.

telemetry.how: Off by default. [otel] in ~/.code/config.toml: exporter = "otlp-http" (endpoint, headers, protocol json|binary) or "otlp-grpc", environment, log_user_prompt=false. Docs and source cover LOG EVENTS only (codex.conversation_starts, codex.api_request, codex.sse_event, codex.user_prompt, codex.tool_decision, codex.tool_result), service.name = originator (code_cli_rs); no traces or metrics exporter in code-rs/otel/src/config.rs. The 0.6.195 release binary contains the code_otel target and codex.conversation_starts string, so it is compiled in. Source-built copies need the `otel` cargo feature. Event names keep the codex.* prefix.

sources.claim: Turn boundary records exist in the rollout: wire names task_started / task_complete (v1 wire, turn_started/turn_complete accepted), plus turn_aborted
sources.evidence: code-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs `#[serde(rename = "task_started", alias = "turn_started")] TurnStarted`, `rename = "task_complete", alias = "turn_complete"`, `TurnAborted`; core/src/codex/streaming.rs:2534 emits EventMsg::TaskStarted; codex/events.rs persist_event -> RolloutRecorder::record_events for every event that passes should_persist_event_msg. sources.claim: Approval and question events ARE persisted (opposite of upstream Codex, where they are not)
sources.evidence: code-rs/core/src/rollout/policy.rs should_persist_event_msg: `!matches!(ev, EventMsg::ImageGenerationBegin(_) | EventMsg::AgentMessageDelta(_) | EventMsg::AgentReasoningDelta(_) | EventMsg::AgentReasoningRawContentDelta(_))`; ExecApprovalRequest, ApplyPatchApprovalRequest and RequestUserInput are variants of core/src/protocol.rs EventMsg and are not in the exclusion list. TaskLifecycle (which has an AwaitingExternalInput phase emitted around request_user_input in codex/streaming.rs:5391) is dropped by event_msg_to_protocol and never written.

notes: Not verified-locally: Every Code is not installed and no turn was watched, so every process shape and the lsof-to-rollout mapping is from source, docs and static inspection of the release binary. One process is one session (the TUI is in-process). There is no sleep inhibitor, so the best per-session working check is the rollout tail (open task_started, recent write, pid alive) plus a direct shell child; an approval or question wait shows as an exec_approval_request / request_user_input record at the tail. Name collision: a bare argv[0] basename `code` is kept in `names` because the Homebrew tap installs the binary as bin/code. The VS Code app's own `code` is a shell script (argv[0] bash) and does not match, but the standalone VS Code CLI is a native binary called `code` (`code tunnel`, `code serve-web`): those subcommands and the extension flags are vetoed in exclude_args, though `code -r .` from that binary would still be misread as an idle session. Confirm on first live run. Paths with spaces break argv[0] (probe splits on spaces). Prompts passed as argv are split into words and a word equal to an excluded token (for example `login`, `preview`, `cloud`) vetoes the TUI match. `code apply`, `code debug` and `code help` are not excluded and would show as brief idle sessions. `code e` (exec alias) is not matched by the exec surface (args_contain is a substring test on `exec`), so it falls to the TUI surface and is labelled tui; the signals are the same. Auto Drive runs many turns with a coordinator model call between them; between turns no task_started is open, so use the pid file ~/.code/auto-drive/pid-<pid>.json (present for the whole run; never read its goal or command fields: both carry the goal text) to keep such a session working. `code auto` is headless (exec path), labelled tui because the exec surface cannot match it. tool_children can over-report while a model-started long-running shell command (dev server) is still a direct child.
